extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent prosecutors/attorneys referencing MPEP form paragraph usage)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on which MPEP form paragraphs to use for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 (AIA and pre‑AIA), including when prior art is disqualified, joint inventors/ownership presumptions, provisional rejections, and required statutory citations. Covers procedural insertions and evidentiary showings examiners should require or note.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT publication pre‑Nov 29, 2000 not prior art under pre‑AIA 102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reference is a publication of an international application (PCT), including voluntary U.S. publication under 35 U.S.C. 122 of the national stage or a WIPO (PCT) publication, that has an international filing date prior to November 29, 2000, did not designate the United States or was not published in English by WIPO, do not use this form paragraph. Such a reference is not a prior art reference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e). The reference may be applied under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or (b) as of its publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See form paragraphs 7.08.fti and 7.09.fti for assistance. (This is a rule on determining whether a PCT publication qualifies under pre‑AIA 102(e) or instead as 102(a)/(b) based on filing date, designation, and WIPO English publication.)

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.16.fti Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) Public Use or On Sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) based upon a public use or sale of the invention. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.09.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. (2) A full explanation of the evidence establishing a public use or sale must be provided in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.17.aia 102(a)(1) Rejection Using Prior Art Excepted under 102(b)(2)(C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has provided evidence in this file showing that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed in the prior art reference were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [1] not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, or the subject matter disclosed in the prior art reference was developed and the claimed invention was made by, or on behalf of one or more parties to a joint research agreement in effect not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention. However, although reference [2] has been disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), it is still applicable as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) that cannot be disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may rely on the exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) by a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the subject matter disclosed in the reference was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor; or rely on 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) by evidence of a prior public disclosure via affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(b). Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia and the noted preceding paragraphs. Bracket instructions: insert claim numbers in bracket 1 and full explanation of public use/sale/availability in bracket 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.17.fti Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) Abandonment of Invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) This form paragraph must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.10.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. (2) In bracket 2, insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment of the invention. See MPEP § 2134.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.18.aia Rejection, Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) as being [2] by [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Use only for an application/patent examined under AIA where the claims contain or contained an effective filing date before March 16, 2013 or a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) to any patent/application that contains such a claim. (2) In bracket 1 insert claim numbers under rejection. (3) In bracket 2 insert either '--clearly anticipated--' or '--anticipated--' with explanation at end. (4) In bracket 3 insert the prior art relied upon. (5) Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.14.aia or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.18.fti Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) Foreign Patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) as being barred by applicants [2]. [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Must be preceded either by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.11.fti or by form paragraph 7.103. (2) In bracket 3 insert explanation of this rejection which must include appropriate dates and how they make the foreign patent available under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d). (3) Refer to MPEP § 2135 for applicable pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d) prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.19.fti Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) Applicant Not the Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) because the applicant did not invent the claimed subject matter. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) This paragraph must be preceded either by paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.13.fti or by paragraph 7.103. (2) In bracket 2 insert an explanation of the supporting evidence establishing that applicant was not the inventor. See MPEP § 2137.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.aia Statement of Statutory Basis, 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of 35 U.S.C. 103: 'A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained, notwithstanding that the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date ... Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 where claims are examined under AIA 102/103; must be preceded by form paragraph 7.03.aia. (2) The statute is not to be cited in all Office actions; required in first actions on the merits employing 35 U.S.C. 103 and final rejections. Where statute is applied but not cited use paragraph 7.103. (3) Use this paragraph only ONCE in a given Office action. (4) Must precede listed 7.20.xx and 7.21.xx paragraphs when used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.fti Statement of Statutory Basis, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotation of pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a): '(a) A patent may not be obtained though the invention is not identically disclosed ... if the differences between the subject matter sought to be patented and the prior art are such that the subject matter as a whole would have been obvious at the time the invention was made to a person having ordinary skill in the art ... Patentability shall not be negatived by the manner in which the invention was made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) The statute is not to be cited in all Office actions; required in first actions on the merits employing pre‑AIA 103(a) and final rejections. Where statute is applied but not cited use paragraph 7.103. (2) Use this form paragraph ONCE in a given Office action. (3) Must precede the pre‑AIA 7.20.xx/7.22.fti paragraphs when used to cite the statute in first actions and final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.01.aia 103 Rejection Using Prior Art Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) (AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has provided evidence in this file showing that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed in the prior art reference were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [1] not later than the effective filing date ... However, although reference [2] has been disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), it is still applicable as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) that cannot be disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome rejection by a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the subject matter was obtained directly/indirectly from the inventor (not prior art under 102(b)(1)(A)) or under 37 CFR 1.130(b) showing prior public disclosure (102(b)(1)(B)). Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Include following 7.20.aia or 7.15.aia where 103 rejection is based on a reference disqualified under 102(b)(2)(C) but still qualifies under 102(a)(1). (3)-(4) Bracket instructions: identify common assignee and disqualified reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.01.fti Pre‑AIA 103(a) Using Prior Art Under Pre‑AIA 102(e),(f),(g) That Is Not Disqualified Under Pre‑AIA 103(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has provided evidence in this file showing that the invention was owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [1] at the time this invention was made, or was subject to a joint research agreement at the time this invention was made. However, reference [2] qualifies as prior art under another subsection of pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102, and therefore is not disqualified as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome applied art by showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed was derived from the inventor of this application (not 'by another'), or by antedating the applied art under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Examiner Note: (1) Include following 7.20.fti in all actions containing pre‑AIA 103(a) rejections using art disqualified under 103(c) by 102(e)/(f)/(g) but qualifying under another section. (2)-(3) Bracket instructions: identify common assignee and disqualified reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.02.aia Joint Inventors, Common Ownership Presumed (AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application currently names joint inventors. In considering patentability of the claims the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time any inventions covered therein were effectively filed absent any evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is advised of the obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out the inventor and effective filing dates of each claim that was not commonly owned at the time a later invention was effectively filed in order for the examiner to consider applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) for any potential 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) prior art against the later invention. Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Must be used in all applications with joint inventors (unless claims are clearly restricted to only one claimed invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.02.fti Joint Inventors, Common Ownership Presumed (pre‑AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: This application currently names joint inventors. In considering patentability of the claims under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), the examiner presumes that the subject matter of the various claims was commonly owned at the time any inventions covered therein were made absent any evidence to the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is advised of obligation under 37 CFR 1.56 to point out inventor and invention dates of each claim not commonly owned at the time a later invention was made so examiner can consider applicability of pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and potential pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C.102(e),(f),(g) prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a). This paragraph must be used in all applications with joint inventors (unless only one claimed invention is presented).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.04.aia 102/103 Rejection Using 102(a)(2) Attempted Disqualification under 102(b)(2)(C) (Common Ownership/Assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has attempted to disqualify reference [1] under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) by showing that the claimed invention was owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [2] at the time the claimed invention was effectively filed. However, applicant has failed to provide a statement that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed were owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person no later than the effective filing date ... and therefore, the reference is not disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file the required evidence to properly disqualify the reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). See MPEP § 706.02(l). Additionally, applicant may overcome the rejection via 37 CFR 1.130(a) (derived from inventor) or 37 CFR 1.130(b) (prior public disclosure). Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Include in all actions containing rejections using 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) prior art where an attempt to disqualify under 102(b)(2)(C) is ineffective. (3)-(4) Bracket instructions: identify applied art and common assignee.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.04.fti Pre‑AIA 103(a) Rejection Using Prior Art Attempted Disqualification Under Pre‑AIA 103(c) (Common Ownership/Assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has attempted to disqualify reference [1] under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by showing that the invention was owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same entity as [2] at the time this invention was made. However, applicant has failed to provide a statement ... and therefore, is not disqualified as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must file required evidence to properly disqualify the reference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c). See MPEP § 706.02(l). Examiner Note: (1) Include in all actions containing rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where attempted disqualification under pre‑AIA 103(c) by common ownership/assignment is ineffective. (2) In brackets 1 and 2 identify the commonly owned applied art (e.g., patent or co‑pending application).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.05.aia 102/103 Rejection Using 102(a)(2) Attempted Disqualification Under 102(b)(2)(C) Using Joint Research Agreement (AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has attempted to disqualify reference [1] under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) by showing that the claimed invention was subject to a joint research agreement in effect not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention. However, applicant has failed to [2]. Applicant must file the missing requirements in order to properly disqualify the reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) and 1.104(c)(4)(ii). Applicant may also overcome the rejection via 37 CFR 1.130(a) (derived from inventor) or 37 CFR 1.130(b) (prior public disclosure). Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Include in all actions containing obviousness or anticipation rejections where an attempt to disqualify 102(a)(2) prior art under 102(b)(2)(C) using joint research agreement provisions is ineffective. (3)-(4) Bracket instructions: identify reference sought to be disqualified and reasons attempt is ineffective (e.g., noncompliance with statutory or CREATE Act rule requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.20.05.fti Pre‑AIA 103(a) Rejection Using Prior Art Attempted Disqualification Under Pre‑AIA 103(c) Using Joint Research Agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant has attempted to disqualify reference [1] under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) by showing that the invention was subject to a joint research agreement at the time this invention was made. However, applicant has failed to [2]. Applicant must file the missing requirements in order to properly disqualify the reference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may overcome the applied art either by showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the invention disclosed therein was derived from the inventor of this application (not 'by another'), or by antedating the applied art under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Examiner Note: (1) Include in all actions containing rejections under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) where an attempt to disqualify under pre‑AIA 103(c) using joint research agreement provisions is ineffective. (2)-(3) Bracket instructions: identify reference sought to be disqualified and reasons attempt is ineffective (e.g., failure to submit required statement or amend specification per CREATE Act rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.aia Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 103
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 where claims are being examined under AIA 102/103; must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Must be preceded by either form paragraph 7.20.aia or 7.103. (3) An explanation of the rejection must follow this form paragraph. See MPEP § 2144. (4) If a provisional 103 rejection based on a copending application that would be prior art under 102(a)(2) if published/patented, use 7.21.01.aia instead. (5)-(7) Bracket instructions for claim numbers, prior art relied upon, and precedence for priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.fti Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: (1) Must be preceded by either form paragraph 7.20.fti or 7.103. (2) An explanation of the rejection must follow; see MPEP § 2144. (3) If the rejection relies upon prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), use pre‑AIPA 102(e) as amended by AIPA to determine reference's prior art date unless reference is a U.S. patent issued from an international application with international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000. See Examiner Notes for 7.12.fti and 7.12.01.fti. (4) If applicability prevents disqualification under pre‑AIA 103(c) then 7.20.01.fti must follow. (5) If provisional pre‑AIA 103(a) based on copending application use 7.21.01.fti instead. (6)-(7) Bracket instructions for claim numbers and prior art reference(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.01.aia Provisional Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 103, Common Assignee/Applicant/Joint Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effectively filed date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published or patented. This provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application. [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained directly/indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B); or (3) a statement pursuant to 102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/assignment or joint research agreement. Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Used to provisionally reject claims not patentably distinct from a copending application having earlier effective filed date and a common assignee/applicant/joint inventor. (3) If claimed invention is fully disclosed in copending application use 7.15.01.aia. (4)-(7) Bracket instructions for claim numbers, application number, type of common relationship, and explanation of obviousness. (8) If not patentably distinct, double patenting rejection should also be made using 8.33 and 8.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.01.fti Provisional Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), Common Assignee/Applicant/Joint Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over copending Application No. [2] which has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if published or patented. This provisional rejection is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application. [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection might be overcome by: (a) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending application was derived from the inventor/joint inventors of this application (not 'by another'); (b) showing a date of invention for the instant application prior to the copending application's effective U.S. filing date under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (c) showing the copending application is disqualified under pre‑AIA 103(c) as prior art. Examiner Note: (1) Used to provisionally reject claims not patentably distinct from disclosure in copending application with earlier U.S. filing date and common assignee/applicant/joint inventor; (2) Use pre‑AIPA 102(e) rules for determining copending application's prior art date as applicable. (3) If claimed invention is fully disclosed use 7.15.01.fti. (4)-(6) Bracket instructions for claim numbers, application number, and type of common relationship. (8)-(9) Additional notes on follow‑on rejections and double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.02.aia Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 103, Common Assignee/Common Applicant/Joint Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effectively filed date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2). [4]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that subject matter was obtained directly/indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor and thus not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A); (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B); or (3) a statement pursuant to 102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/assignment or joint research agreement. Examiner Note: (1) Use only in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia. (2) Use to reject over a reference (patent or published application) with earlier effective date that discloses the claimed invention and ONLY qualifies as prior art under 102(a)(2). If reference qualifies as 102(a)(1) use 7.21.aia instead. (3) Should not be used in applications when reference is disqualified under 102(b)(2)(C) as prior art under 102(a)(2). (4) Bracket instruction: insert explanation of obviousness per MPEP § 2144.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.21.02.fti Rejection, pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a), Common Assignee/Common Applicant/Joint Inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] is/are rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over [2]. The applied reference has a common [3] with the instant application. Based upon the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the reference was derived from the inventor of this application (not 'by another'); (2) showing of a date of invention for the claimed subject matter prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a); or (3) an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131(c) stating current common ownership and that the inventor named in the application is the prior inventor under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 104 together with a terminal disclaimer per 37 CFR 1.321(c). Also see notes on application of pre‑AIPA 102(e) and when to use other paragraphs (7.12.fti, 7.12.01.fti). (4) Bracket instructions for claim numbers and prior art references relied upon.
